promises.credibility: Management's observable track record is mixed and points to mild over-optimism on near-term execution, having missed its reaffirmed FY26 15% revenue growth target at 11.8% [T4.1, T3.1] and repeatedly slipped the closing timeline for the Hyderabad Metro divestment despite signing the SPA [T4.8]. Accountability is also hindered by incomplete follow-through in reported metrics, leaving several past-deadline operational and segment targets—such as FY26 P&M margins [T4.2, T3.2], order inflows [T4.3], NWC-to-sales [T4.4], and data center capacity [T3.7]—unverified, while most FY27 and five-year Lakshya L31 commitments remain too early to judge [T2.2, T1.1, T2.3].

what_they_do.text: Larsen & Toubro Limited operates through a diverse portfolio spanning infrastructure and utilities construction, conventional and green energy projects, and hi-tech manufacturing. The company also provides integrated technology, platforms, and services, alongside retail financial services and real estate development.

customers_and_markets.text: The company's order book has a geographic split of 48% domestic and 52% international, with the Middle East accounting for 71% of its international portfolio.
Private sector demand is a key driver, with the share of private sector orders increasing to 40% of the domestic order book as of June 2026.
The company serves government and public sector enterprises, though their combined share of the domestic order book declined to 30% as of June 2026.

recent_developments.text: Effective April 1, 2026, the company realigned its reporting segments under the Lakshya 2031 Strategic Plan, including the creation of an 'Energy - Green' segment and the separate classification of the 'Realty' business.
The company secured an ultra-mega order under the TenneT North Sea HVDC offshore wind program, accumulating approximately 8 GWs of offshore wind transmission capacity over three quarters.
L&T signed an agreement to divest its entire stake in L&T Metro Rail Hyderabad Limited to the Government of Telangana, with expected completion by September 30, 2026.
The company received a 'Baa1' long-term issuer rating from Moody's Ratings, which is two notches above the sovereign.

bull.text: Group order inflows for Q1 FY27 grew 14% YoY to Rs 1,080 billion, driven by a 27% YoY increase in international orders and strong momentum in offshore wind awards.
The total order book expanded 27% YoY to Rs 7.79 trillion as of June 2026, supported by a healthy Rs 15 trillion prospects pipeline for the remaining nine months of FY27.
Working capital discipline yielded significant results, with the Net Working Capital to Sales ratio improving to 4.9% in June 2026 from 10.1% in June 2025.

bear.text: Management missed its full-year FY26 group revenue growth target of 15%, achieving 11.8% growth (Rs 2,85,874 Cr) due to domestic execution delays and Middle East conflict disruptions.

Group EBITDA margin contracted 2 percentage points YoY to 11% in September 2026, while Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin excluding other income fell 90 basis points YoY to 9.0% due to lower execution and Rs 2.5 billion in ECL provisions.
Financial leverage remains elevated, with a reported Debt/Equity ratio of 1.15x.

watch.text: Completion of the divestment of L&T Metro Rail Hyderabad Limited to the Government of Telangana by the revised target date of September 30, 2026.
Re-acceleration of project awarding activity in the Middle East starting in Q2 FY27 to support full-year order inflow growth guidance of 10-12%.
Finalization and disclosure of the Lakshya FY27 plan capex outlays expected during Q2 FY27.
